    def runtime_reclaim_stale_claims(self, reclaiming_node_id: str, *, stale_after_seconds: float = 15.0) -> list[str]:
        """A real, previously-missing safety mechanism: a task claimed by
        runtime_claim_task() but never completed (the claiming node died or
        stalled before ever calling emit_node_result()) was stuck forever --
        confirmed empirically: no code path anywhere resets status='CLAIMED'
        back to 'OPEN'. This method lets ANY currently-healthy node scan for
        exactly that situation and safely reclaim it.

        A task is eligible for reclaim only if BOTH:
        (a) its status is 'CLAIMED' AND its claiming node_id is either (i) not
            present at all in the `nodes` table, or (ii) present with
            healthy=0, or (iii) present with healthy=1 but
            last_seen_ts older than `stale_after_seconds` (a node can go
            unhealthy without ever calling runtime_heartbeat(healthy=False) --
            e.g. a hard SIGKILL never gets to update its own row at all, so a
            stale last_seen_ts on an otherwise 'healthy=1' row is the ONLY
            real signal for that specific failure mode -- do not assume
            healthy=0 will always be set).
        (b) NO packet in `outbox` currently references this exact task_id in
            its decoded payload (payload.task_id == this task_id) -- if a
            result was already emitted and is just waiting for a coordinator
            to drain it, reclaiming would be WRONG (duplicate work, and a
            race against the coordinator committing the real result). Decode
            each outbox row's packet_json (json.loads), read
            packet['payload'].get('task_id'), compare.

        On finding an eligible task: reset it in the SAME transaction (status
        back to 'OPEN', claimed_by back to NULL), advance the epoch via
        self._bump(con) exactly once per commit (standard pattern already
        used elsewhere in this file), and return the list of task_ids that
        were reclaimed (empty list if none were eligible). Log nothing beyond
        what the caller can already see in the returned list and via a fresh
        snapshot() afterward -- do not add a new table for this.

        Use a single connect()+BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction for the whole scan
        (read tasks+nodes+outbox, decide, write) so this is race-safe against
        another node doing the same reclaim scan concurrently -- exactly the
        same real multi-process safety guarantee every other mutating method
        in this file already has. If the scan finds zero eligible tasks,
        still commit cleanly (or rollback is fine too) and return [].

        reclaiming_node_id is accepted as a parameter for API symmetry with
        the rest of this file's methods (they all take a node_id) and MAY be
        used to log which node performed the reclaim if you add that to the
        return value as a list of dicts instead of plain strings -- your
        choice, but keep the return type consistent and documented in the
        docstring you write.
        """

A task claimed by a node whose last_seen_ts is old (use monkeypatched time.time() or just sleep past a tiny stale_after_seconds like 0.05) but whose healthy flag was never explicitly set to False (simulating a hard-killed process that never got to report its own death) IS ALSO reclaimed -- this is the main real-world case this fix targets.
